identity.title: Negative Role of the Receptor-Like Kinase GbMIK2 in Regulating Cotton Verticillium Wilt Resistance.

content.abstract: The leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinases (LRR-RLKs) function in multifaceted processes in plant growth, reproduction, cell differentiation and immunity. However, the role of the RLK gene MIK2 (Male discoverer 1-Interacting receptor-like Kinase 2) in regulating cotton resistance to Verticillium dahliae remains unclear. Virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) of GbMIK2 or CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knocking out of GhMIK2 increased cotton resistance to V. dahliae infection, while ectopic expression of GbMIK2 in Arabidopsis thaliana decreased the plant resistance, indicating a negative role of GbMIK2 in cotton Verticillium wilt resistance. GbMIK2 interacted with its co-receptor GbBAK1 during V. dahliae infection in the initial immune response, resulting in activation of the MAPK cascade. GbMIK2 interacted in the membrane and nucleus with GbOCP3, which also plays a negative role in Verticillium wilt resistance. Both GbMIK2 and GbOCP3 are located in the membrane and nucleus. Their interaction blocked the reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst and jasmonic acid (JA)-mediated resistance to V. dahliae, resulting in suppression of cotton resistance to Verticillium wilt. These results collectively indicate that GbMIK2, interacting with GbOCP3, acts as a negative regulator in modulating cotton Verticillium wilt resistance, providing new insights to the understanding of mechanisms of RLKs in cotton disease resistance.
